definitions.explanation: Among the very best or most prominent in a given category. Used to describe something or someone that ranks at the top. Literally means 'bending the fingers' (to count the best).

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}{屈指|くっし}の{名門|めいもん}{大学|だいがく}だ。
examples.english: It is one of Japan's leading prestigious universities.

examples.japanese: {世界|せかい}{屈指|くっし}の{技術力|ぎじゅつりょく}を{持|も}つ{企業|きぎょう}だ。
examples.english: It is a company with world-class technical capabilities.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}は{国内|こくない}{屈指|くっし}の{米|こめ}どころとして{知|し}られている。
examples.english: This region is known as one of the country's leading rice-producing areas.

notes:
GRAMMAR:
{屈指|くっし} is used as a modifier with の. The typical pattern is X{屈指|くっし}のY (one of the top Y in X), where X is a scope (country, world, region) and Y is the thing being praised.

ETYMOLOGY:
Literally "bending the fingers" — the idea of counting the best on one's fingers, implying there are so few at the top that you can count them.

COLLOCATIONS:
- {日本|にほん}{屈指|くっし}の — one of Japan's top/leading
- {世界|せかい}{屈指|くっし}の — world-class, world-leading
- {国内|こくない}{屈指|くっし}の — one of the country's foremost
- {業界|ぎょうかい}{屈指|くっし}の — leading in the industry
